questions.q: Why can't a vulnerability scan limit itself to the application code you personally wrote?
options: Scanners are only capable of reading application source files, never compiled binaries
A final image is mostly other people's code — base OS packages, the language runtime, and third-party dependencies — any of which can carry a known vulnerability
Application code is never a source of vulnerabilities, only OS packages are
Vulnerability scanning only applies to images larger than 1 GB
questions.explain: An image stacks your base OS, runtime, and every dependency underneath your own code, and a vulnerability can enter through any of those layers.

options: A cataloged, published identifier for a specific known security flaw in a specific package or version
A proprietary Docker Hub feature with no public database behind it
A command that rebuilds an image from scratch
A type of Kubernetes deployment strategy
questions.explain: CVE stands for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures — a published, catalogued identifier (tracked in databases like the NVD) for a specific disclosed security flaw.

questions.q: In `trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --exit-code 1 --ignore-unfixed myapp:1.4.2`, what does --ignore-unfixed accomplish?
options: It disables the severity filter entirely
It deletes the image if any vulnerability is found
It avoids failing the build over a CVE that currently has no available fix, since blocking the release wouldn't change the outcome
It raises the severity of every finding to Critical
questions.explain: --ignore-unfixed excludes findings with no patched version yet from the pass/fail gate, since failing the build can't resolve something with no fix available.

questions.q: What does an SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) actually contain?
options: The git commit history of the application's source repository
Only the names of packages that currently have a Critical CVE
A log of every docker run command ever executed against the image
A complete inventory of every package and version present in the image, independent of whether anything is currently flagged as vulnerable
questions.explain: An SBOM, generated by tools like syft, is a full package-and-version inventory of the image — useful for immediately checking exposure the moment a new CVE is published.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between Trivy and Docker Scout as described in this lesson?
options: Docker Scout can only scan Windows containers
Trivy can only be run inside GitHub Actions, never locally
Both answer the same question — which known CVEs does this exact image contain — using different scan engines and databases, which is why teams often run both
Trivy and Docker Scout are the exact same tool under two different names
questions.explain: Trivy (Aqua Security) and Docker Scout (Docker's built-in tool) both fingerprint image contents against CVE data, but use different engines, which is why some teams run more than one for coverage.
